package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp installers for both Windows and macOS were trojanized to include a multi-stage malware loader. The compromised application, signed with a legitimate code signing certificate, downloads and executes additional payloads from external sources, ultimately leading to the deployment of an information-stealing infostealer DLL. This behavior is not expected in legitimate software and constitutes a supply chain attack affecting all users of the compromised versions.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, upon application launch or during normal operation

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The trojanized binary contains code that, after launch, downloads ICO files from github.com/IconStorages/images, extracts appended base64-encoded payloads, and writes/loads a next-stage DLL.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads ICO files from a remote GitHub repository, extracts and decodes base64-encoded data appended to these files, writes the decoded payload to disk, and loads it as a DLL for further execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing code from external sources, especially from image files hosted on GitHub, is highly abnormal for a VOIP application and is a common technique used to evade detection and deliver additional malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate VOIP applications are expected to load only signed, trusted code included in the installer or from official update channels. Downloading and executing code hidden in image files from third-party repositories is never expected or acceptable.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may download signed updates from official vendor servers, but do not download or execute arbitrary code hidden in image files from unrelated third-party repositories.
key_indicators: Downloads ICO files from github.com/IconStorages/images at runtime
Extracts and decodes appended base64 data from image files
Writes decoded payload to disk and loads it as a DLL
Dynamic DLL loading from files not present in the original installer

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, after stage 1 payload execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The loaded DLL acts as an infostealer, harvesting system information, browser data, and potentially credentials, then exfiltrating this data to attacker-controlled infrastructure (e.g., akamaitechcloudservices.com, azureonlinestorage.com, msedgepackageinfo.com, etc.).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects sensitive information from the infected system, including browser data and credentials, and sends this data via HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled domains.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating user data, such as browser credentials and system information, is a hallmark of infostealer malware and is never legitimate in a VOIP client.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A VOIP client should not access browser data, credentials, or send sensitive information to unknown external servers. Such actions are strictly outside the scope of normal application behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason for a VOIP client to access or exfiltrate browser data or credentials; this behavior is always malicious in this context.
key_indicators: Accesses browser data and credentials from the local system
Sends collected data to non-3CX, attacker-controlled domains
Uses HTTPS POST requests for data exfiltration
Targets specific domains associated with attacker infrastructure

attack_chain.action: User installs or updates 3CXDesktopApp with a trojanized installer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code embedded in the application binary

attack_chain.action: Trojanized application, upon launch, downloads ICO files from GitHub and extracts/decodes a next-stage payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Loading and execution of the next-stage infostealer DLL

attack_chain.action: Extracted DLL is loaded and executed, harvesting sensitive data and exfiltrating it to attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data theft and potential further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Application downloads ICO or image files from github.com/IconStorages/images or other non-standard sources at runtime
Extraction and decoding of base64 data appended to image files
Dynamic loading of DLLs not present in the original installer package
Unexpected HTTPS POST requests to non-3CX domains associated with attacker infrastructure
Access to browser credential stores or sensitive user data by 3CXDesktopApp process
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for 3CXDesktopApp processes making network requests to GitHub repositories or the listed suspicious domains, especially for ICO/image file downloads. Detect extraction and execution of code from downloaded image files by monitoring for base64 decoding and DLL loading activity. Flag any dynamic DLL loading from files not present in the original installer. Alert on any exfiltration of browser data or credentials to non-3CX domains via HTTPS POST. Correlate with known malicious file hashes and installer filenames to identify compromised installations.
